name: crt-screen
title: CRT Screen
description: A scene behind curved tube glass: barrel distortion, an RGB phosphor mask, scanlines that bow with the picture, bloom around bright text and corners that run off into black. Runs its WebGL shader over its own built-in scene (a render queue list; title, rows and background from variables), not over the host video. The only motion is a 1 % brightness breath, so it holds as a look.
useWhen: Something should read as shown on a tube rather than rendered flat: retro terminals, arcade beats, an old dashboard being demoed.
The content is high contrast, bright text on a dark field, which the phosphor mask and bloom were built for.
avoidWhen: The story is worn tape rather than a monitor: use vhs-filter.
It should read as photographed rather than displayed: use camera-lens.
The tube should switch off rather than run: use tv-power-off.
Content sits close to the frame edge: the barrel warp pushes the corners into the dark rim.
author: Remocn

variables.label: Rows
variables.description: Rows of the list as name | status, separated by semicolons (up to 5).
variables.default: intro-scene.mp4 | Done; feature-tour.mp4 | Rendering; pricing-outro.mp4 | Queued

variables.label: Background
variables.description: Background of the scene on the glass.

variables.label: Curvature
variables.description: How far the tube bulges. At 0 the frame stays flat and nothing is clipped at the corners.

variables.label: Scanlines
variables.description: Strength of the horizontal lines, which bow with the picture.

variables.label: Mask scale
variables.description: Width of one phosphor stripe in frame pixels; a triad is three times this. Low reads as a fine grille, high as a coarse arcade tube.

variables.label: Vignette
variables.description: How hard the picture falls off toward the rim.

variables.label: Resolution
variables.description: Share of the frame size the shader is drawn at, then scaled up. The phosphor mask needs 1; lower renders faster but softens it.
